subject: Civic Education
competence: Names the public services provided for the area identifying them and appreciates their contribution to human development.
lesson: Presents information about other public services provided by the government: Government Services Legislative Mock Expo & Presentation
unique_learning_outcome: Presents information about other public services provided by the government.
the_entrance: 5-minute introduction: The teacher welcomes the class and projects a vibrant visual slide of a local Divisional Secretariat office interacting with citizens in Sri Lanka. As a motivational hook, the teacher challenges the 6 student groups: 'Today, our classroom transforms into the National Government Services Expo. You are senior information officers representing various ministries. Can your team pitch your assigned public service so clearly that visiting citizens immediately understand its direct benefit to our community?' Student groups eagerly gather their ministry files, assign roles for their upcoming expo presentations, and review their assigned service portfolios with their team leaders.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher circulates among the 6 groups, acting as a lead facilitator to assist teams in structuring their 2-minute oral presentation key points and organizing chalk diagrams. The teacher asks probing scaffold questions such as: 'Which specific citizen needs does your ministry service address first, and how will you represent this clearly on the chalkboard?'
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Team leaders and secretaries collaborate to draft a concise 2-minute presentation outline on chart paper, while civic investigators verify facts against textbook guidelines and timekeepers check pacing. Group members practice their speaking parts and assign chalkboard sketching duties to prepare for the upcoming expo rotation.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Chart paper, colored markers, and ministry fact sheets on fisheries support, cooperative development, and cultural affairs.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher manages the strict presentation timer, ensuring each of the 6 teams delivers their 2-minute ministerial briefing without interruption while moderating the peer Q&A session. The teacher prompts audience groups to ask critical, clarifying questions and guides constructive peer evaluation after each ministry showcase.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Group spokespersons step forward sequentially to present their ministry's public services to the class while illustrating key functions using chalkboard diagrams. Meanwhile, visiting audience groups take concise notes in their notebooks and actively pose probing inquiries regarding service accessibility and community benefits.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_method: Legislative Mock Expo & Interactive Presentation Showcase
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Chalkboard, student notebooks, and spokesperson role cards.

summary: In a 2-minute plenary synthesis, the teacher and students consolidate key discoveries, highlighting how diverse government ministries—such as fisheries, cooperatives, and cultural affairs—collaborate to deliver essential public services that uplift community life across Sri Lanka.
assessment_and_feedback_whole_lesson: Formative evaluation is conducted continuously through peer questioning during the mock expo, accuracy of chalkboard presentation outlines, and the depth of student notes recorded in notebooks regarding government public service functions.
post_activity: 5-minute in-class assignment: Creative Rhyming Verse Recitation: In pairs, students compose and recite a 2-line original rhyming verse summarizing the core value of government public services presented during the expo (e.g., 'From fisheries aid to cultural care, government public services are everywhere!'). The teacher invites selected pairs to perform their verses aloud and provides immediate positive reinforcement.
attachments: Ministry Information Fact Sheets on Fisheries, Cooperative Development, and Cultural Affairs

Approach: Student groups take on the persona of government ministry information officers hosting an interactive community exhibition to present information on diverse public services to visiting citizens.
Student task: Each group prepares a 2-minute oral presentation accompanied by chalkboard diagrams outlining a specific set of public services (e.g., fisheries support, cooperative development, cultural affairs) and presents it to the rest of the class.
Teacher facilitation: The teacher manages the strict presentation schedule, ensuring each of the 6 teams gets an equal opportunity to present while prompting audience groups to ask clarifying questions.
Expected output: A structured public service presentation outline recorded in student notebooks and delivered verbally by spokespersons.
Grouping: 6 teams (6 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer
